blocks.content: Pyroclastic flows are among the most lethal of all volcanic hazards due to their extreme temperatures and extraordinary speeds.

rows: Incandescent ash, pumice, and toxic gases
Extremely rapid (up to 700 km/h) gravity-driven flows
Immediate surrounding slopes and proximal valleys
Volcanic ash, mud, water, and debris
High-velocity fluid mudflows following river valleys
Downstream river channels and low-lying plains
Pulverized rock fragments and glass particles
Widespread regional airspace, farmlands, and urban roofs

items: Frequently tested: Distinction between Pyroclastic Flows (high-temperature dry gas/ash) and Lahars (water-saturated volcanic mudflows).
Barren Island in the Andaman Sea is India's only active volcano, whereas Narcondam is considered a dormant/extinct volcanic island.
Sulfur dioxide released into the stratosphere forms sulfate aerosols that reflect solar radiation, leading to global volcanic winter effects.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways: Volcanic Hazards
items: Pyroclastic flows are high-density mixtures of scorching gas, ash, and volcanic rock moving at speeds exceeding several hundred kilometers per hour.
Lahars are catastrophic volcanic mudflows formed when volcanic debris mixes with heavy rainfall, river water, or melted snow and ice.
Volcanic ash consists of microscopic pulverized rock and glass, posing severe hazards to commercial aviation, public health, and electrical grids.
Volcanic gas emissions contain sulfur dioxide, carbon dioxide, and hydrogen fluoride, contributing to acid rain and localized asphyxiation.
The Volcanic Explosivity Index (VEI) measures eruption magnitude from 0 (non-explosive) to 8 (mega-colossal super-eruptions).
